w: The downtown branch alone circulates more items each year than any other single library location in the United States, over four million annually from 542,527 square feet of stacks. Across 41 locations the system holds about 9.6 million volumes, the country's second-largest public library collection.
s: America's busiest single library, in one building
_facts: Downtown location: 542,527 sq ft, most annual circulation of any single US library
System-wide holdings of about 9.6 million volumes, 2nd-largest public library collection in the US
Largest e-book holdings of any US public library
Five-star Library Journal rating every year since 2013

w: Built during the Civil War for $275,000 and modeled on Granada's Alhambra, the Plum Street Temple was dedicated in 1866 in honor of Rabbi Isaac Mayer Wise, a founder of American Reform Judaism. It stands across from St. Peter in Chains Cathedral, among the oldest synagogue buildings still in use in the US.
s: An Alhambra-inspired synagogue built during the Civil War
_facts: Dedicated 1866, cost $275,000 (about $6.05 million in 2025)
Designed by James Keys Wilson, modeled on the Alhambra in Granada
Honors Rabbi Isaac Mayer Wise, a founder of American Reform Judaism
National Historic Landmark since 1975

w: Samuel Hannaford's 1893 Richardsonian Romanesque city hall replaced an 1852 predecessor and cost $1.61 million to build, of which he was paid $54,000 as architect. Stained-glass windows depict Cincinnatus and the city's founding; the marble stairways came from Italy and Tennessee, the granite columns from Vermont.
s: A Romanesque city hall of imported marble and granite
_facts: Completed 1893, designed by Samuel Hannaford, cost $1.61 million
Replaced an 1852 city hall on the same site
Stone from Wisconsin, Ohio, Missouri and Indiana; marble from Italy and Tennessee; granite from Vermont
On the National Register of Historic Places since 1972

w: Cass Gilbert designed this 1913 tower for Union Central Life on the site of a Chamber of Commerce building lost to fire two years earlier, using Thompson-Starrett, the same contractor as his Woolworth Building in New York. At 495 feet it was Cincinnati's tallest until 1930, briefly the fifth-tallest building on Earth.
s: Cass Gilbert's Cincinnati answer to the Woolworth Building
_facts: Completed 1913, designed by Cass Gilbert
Fifth-tallest building in the world on completion
Cincinnati's tallest building from 1913 to 1930, when Carew Tower opened
Shared contractor, Thompson-Starrett, with Gilbert's Woolworth Building

w: Completed just before the 1990 World Series, this 35-story tower was shaped by its architects to resemble a lighthouse, echoing the E.W. Scripps Company motto, 'Give light and the people will find their own way.' It houses Scripps's headquarters and doubles as the 'studio' for its automated Ion Media stations.
s: A skyscraper built to look like a lighthouse
_facts: Completed 1990, 468 feet tall, 35 stories
Designed to resemble a lighthouse, tied to Scripps's motto
Cincinnati's tallest building added between Carew Tower (1931) and Great American Tower (2011)
Houses the headquarters of the E.W. Scripps Company

w: At 733 acres, Spring Grove is the third-largest cemetery in the United States, behind only Calverton and Abraham Lincoln National. Founded in 1844 and run as a nonprofit arboretum as much as a burial ground, it earned National Historic Landmark status for its landscape design and notable burials.
s: America's third-largest cemetery, also a working arboretum
_facts: 733 acres, third-largest cemetery in the US
Founded 1844
Nonprofit cemetery and arboretum
National Historic Landmark for its age, architecture and notable burials
